body.statement:
For every \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\), put \(r=|D\setminus T|\).  There is a universal \(C>0\) such that \(\mathsf A(G,T,e,\delta)\) returns, with total symbolic error probability at most \(\delta\), exactly one of the following four mutually exclusive outputs.
\[
\begin{array}{lll}
r=0,\ d_e(G)<\infty:
&\displaystyle
(\operatorname{tree},d_e(G),(\rho_i)_{i=1}^{d_e(G)}),
& d_e(G)\in\{1,2\},\\[3pt]
r=0,\ d_e(G)=\infty:
&(\operatorname{tree},\infty),&\\[3pt]
r>0,\ d_e(G)<\infty:
&\displaystyle
(\operatorname{algebraic},\mathcal J_{G,e},2^{|D|-n+2}),
&\displaystyle d_e(G)\leq2^{|D|-n+2}\leq2^{k+1},\\[3pt]
r>0,\ d_e(G)=\infty:
&(\infty,\mathcal N_{G,e}).&
\end{array}
\]
In the first case, the \(\rho_i\) are all the fractional affine square-root expressions returned by the complete tree algorithm and exhaust the generic complex queried-coordinate values.  In the third case, \(\mathcal J_{G,e}\) is a Jacobian-rank transcript certifying algebraicity, but the output does not claim to compute \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\).  In the fourth case, \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\) certifies that the queried-coordinate projection of the integral generic fiber is dominant onto \(\mathbb A^1_{K_G}\).  In \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\), the construction time and certificate length are at most \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\).
body.justification: The unconditional operational result is an exact algebraic-versus-transcendental tag with a certified finite-degree ceiling; it no longer launders an absent eliminant.
body.gap: Neither general polynomial-space identification nor extensional quadratic-core reduction constructs the bounded source-prime chart needed for exact finite output.
body.consumer: fasttreeid can safely report finite algebraic ambiguity versus an infinite queried projection; exact degree and polynomial output require the conditional chart theorem.
body.proof_tex:
Let
\[
r=|D\setminus T|.
\]
Because \(r\) is read directly from the supplied graph, dispatching on \(r=0\) or \(r>0\) is deterministic and exhaustive.

Suppose first that \(r=0\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}class\mbox{-}algorithm\mbox{-}transfer}\), the graph is in exactly the published tree-shaped mixed-graph class, including arbitrary bidirected support.  Run the transferred tree algorithm with failure tolerance \(\delta\).  If \(d_e(G)<\infty\), that lemma proves
\[
d_e(G)\in\{1,2\}
\]
and proves that its returned list \((\rho_i)_{i=1}^{d_e(G)}\) exhausts the generic complex coordinate values.  The dispatcher therefore returns
\[
(\operatorname{tree},d_e(G),(\rho_i)_{i=1}^{d_e(G)}).
\]
If \(d_e(G)=\infty\), the same lemma proves that the published procedure reports the infinite case, and the dispatcher returns \((\operatorname{tree},\infty)\).  These are the first two stated outputs, with symbolic error probability at most \(\delta\).

It remains to analyze \(r>0\).  Put
\[
u=(\lambda_D,\omega_B,\omega_{\mathrm{diag}})
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
N=|D|+|B|+n,
\]
so that, by the definition of \(L\),
\[
L=\mathbb C(u_1,\ldots,u_N).
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:acyclic}\), there is a topological ordering in which \(\Lambda\) is strictly triangular.  Thus \(\Lambda^n=0\), and direct multiplication gives
\[
(I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}=I_n+\Lambda+\cdots+\Lambda^{n-1}.
\]
Consequently every entry of \((I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}\) is a polynomial of degree at most \(n-1\) in \(\lambda_D\).  Since every entry of \(\Omega\) is linear in \((\omega_B,\omega_{\mathrm{diag}})\), each distinct covariance coordinate
\[
s_{ij}(u):=\phi_G(\sigma_{ij})
=\bigl[(I_n-\Lambda)^{-\mathsf T}\Omega(I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}\bigr]_{ij}
\]
is a polynomial of total degree at most
\[
(n-1)+1+(n-1)=2n-1.
\]
Repeated matrix multiplication constructs all these polynomials by arithmetic circuits of size polynomial in \(n\).

Let \(s=(s_{ij}:i\leq j)\), let \(J_0=\partial s/\partial u\), and let \(J_1\) be obtained by adjoining to \(J_0\) the row \(\partial\lambda_e/\partial u\).  The entries of \(J_0\) have degree at most \(2n-2\), and the added row has degree zero.

We prove the rank criterion used by the dispatcher.  Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\in L\), set \(F=\mathbb C(a_1,\ldots,a_m)\), and choose a maximal algebraically independent subfamily \(b_1,\ldots,b_q\) of the \(a_i\).  Then \(b_1,\ldots,b_q\) is a transcendence basis of \(F/\mathbb C\).  Extend it by \(c_1,\ldots,c_ell\) to a transcendence basis of \(L/\mathbb C\).  Since \(L\) is finitely generated, the extension
\[
L/\mathbb C(b_1,\ldots,b_q,c_1,\ldots,c_ell)
\]
is finite algebraic, and it is separable because the characteristic is zero.

For each \(j\), the derivation of the displayed rational-function field that sends \(b_j\) to \(1\) and all other \(b\)'s and \(c\)'s to zero extends uniquely to \(L\).  Indeed, if \(v\) is algebraic with minimal polynomial \(g(t)=\sum_h g_h t^h\), differentiating \(g(v)=0\) forces
\[
g'(v)\,dv=-\sum_h v^h\,d g_h,
\]
and separability gives \(g'(v)\neq0\).  Applying the extended derivations to any relation \(\sum_j q_j\,db_j=0\), with \(q_j\in L\), yields \(q_j=0\) for every \(j\).  Thus \(db_1,\ldots,db_q\) are linearly independent over \(L\).

Conversely, each \(a_i\) is algebraic over \(\mathbb C(b_1,\ldots,b_q)\).  Differentiating its separable minimal polynomial expresses \(da_i\) in the \(L\)-span of \(db_1,\ldots,db_q\).  Since the \(b_j\) themselves are among the \(a_i\), we conclude
\[
\dim_L\operatorname{span}_L\{da_1,\ldots,da_m\}
=q
=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}F.
\]

Apply this identity first to the covariance polynomials and then to those polynomials together with \(\lambda_e\).  The rows of the two Jacobians are the coordinate vectors of the corresponding differentials in the basis \(du_1,\ldots,du_N\).  Using the definition \(K_G=\mathbb C(s_{ij}:i,j\in V)\), we obtain
\[
\operatorname{rank}_LJ_0=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}K_G,
\qquad
\operatorname{rank}_LJ_1
=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}K_G(\lambda_e).
\]
Adjoining one element raises transcendence degree by zero precisely when that element is algebraic and otherwise raises it by one.  Therefore
\[
\operatorname{rank}_LJ_1=\operatorname{rank}_LJ_0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\lambda_e\text{ is algebraic over }K_G,
\]
whereas \(\operatorname{rank}_LJ_1=\operatorname{rank}_LJ_0+1\) is equivalent to transcendence.

The dispatcher evaluates both Jacobians at independently sampled exact source points and computes their ranks by exact Gaussian elimination.  There are at most \(n(n+1)/2+1\leq n^2+1\) rows and at most
\[
N=|D|+|B|+n\leq n(n-1)+n=n^2
\]
columns.  Hence every relevant minor has size at most \(n^2+1\) and total degree at most
\[
(n^2+1)(2n-2)\leq2n^3.
\]
Choose every source coordinate independently and uniformly from a finite rational set \(S\) with
\[
|S|\geq \left\lceil\frac{4n^3}{\delta}\right\rceil.
\]
An evaluated rank never exceeds the generic rank.  If the evaluated rank is smaller, a fixed nonzero generic maximal minor has vanished at the sampled point.  By \(\mathrm{lem:schwartz\mbox{-}zippel\mbox{-}bound}\), this event has probability at most
\[
\frac{2n^3}{|S|}\leq\frac{\delta}{2}
\]
for each Jacobian.  A union bound shows that both evaluated ranks equal their generic ranks with probability at least \(1-\delta\).  On this event the displayed rank criterion gives the correct algebraic or transcendental tag.  The exact evaluation points, pivot positions, and nonzero evaluated pivot minors form the transcript \(\mathcal J_{G,e}\).

If the augmented rank is larger, then \(\lambda_e\) is transcendental over \(K_G\), so the homomorphism
\[
K_G[t]\longrightarrow A_K,
\qquad
t\longmapsto\lambda_e,
\]
is injective.  By \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\), \(A_K\) is an integral \(K_G\)-algebra with fraction field \(L\).  The injection therefore induces a dominant morphism
\[
\operatorname{Spec}(A_K)\longrightarrow\mathbb A^1_{K_G}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\dim A_K
=\operatorname{trdeg}_{K_G}\operatorname{Frac}(A_K)
=\operatorname{trdeg}_{K_G}L\geq1,
\]
because \(L\) contains \(\lambda_e\), which is transcendental over \(K_G\).  The augmented pivot minor together with the two rank transcripts is thus the asserted dominance certificate \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\), and the fourth output is correct.

If the ranks agree, then \(d_e(G)<\infty\).  The already established \(\mathrm{thm:orientation\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\) gives
\[
d_e(G)\leq2^{|D|-n+2}\leq2^{k+1}.
\]
Thus the third output is correct.  This step supplies only a degree ceiling: neither the rank computation nor the bound constructs \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\).

Finally, the tree branch is randomized polynomial time by \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}class\mbox{-}algorithm\mbox{-}transfer}\).  On the positive-excess branch, nilpotent matrix summation, circuit differentiation, exact evaluations, and Gaussian elimination require polynomially many arithmetic operations and transcript entries in \(n\).  Sampling uses \(O(\log n+\log(1/\delta))\) bits per coordinate, with bit complexity charged separately in \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\).  Since \(n\geq2\) and \(k\geq0\), one universal \(C>0\) bounds both branch complexities by
\[
n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta)).
\]
Only one branch is executed, so its error probability is the dispatcher's total error probability.  This proves all four cases and the stated complexity and certificate-length bounds.
